newsitem.title: POLAND: FORECAST-Polish 52-wk, 13-wk T-bill yield seen down.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST-Polish 52-wk, 13-wk T-bill yield seen down.

text.p: Banks expect the average yield on Poland's benchmark 52-week T-bill to fall to 17.76 percent at the end of 1997 against 19.97 percent at the last primary sale, a Reuters poll of the country's 24 largest banks showed.
Last month, banks saw the benchmark yield falling to 17.53 percent by year-end. The end-1997 forecasts ranged from 16.50 to 19.10 percent.

Banks expected the 52-week average yield would ease to 17.39 percent in February 1998 with a range of forecasts of 15.4 to 19.1 percent. They expected the yield to rise to 20.08 percent on average at the end of the month with a forecast range from 19.9 to 21.0 percent.

The average yield on the 13-week T-bill was also seen falling to 17.34 percent by year-end from 19.60 percent at the last primary auction, the poll showed. Last month banks expected a deeper yield fall to 17.1 percent.
The 13-week T-bill yield forecast is a mean average of banks' predictions ranging from 16.30 percent to 18.80 percent. @
The yield was seen falling to 16.99 percent in February 1998 with a forecast range between 15.2 and 18.8 percent after rising to 19.70 percent this month with a range from 19.4 to 20.3 percent.
